children: Australia’s Westpac–Melbourne Institute Consumer Sentiment Index fell 4.7% mom to a six-month low of 80.4 in October 2026, slowing from a 5.2% decline in the prior month while marking a second straight month of decline.

Confidence remained under pressure from higher fuel and interest rates, as views on household finances weakened, with assessments of finances over the past year falling 8.0% to 66.9, while expectations for the next 12 months declined 6.4% to 88.4.
Economic sentiment was also subdued, with the one-year outlook slipping 1.6% to 78.3 and the five-year outlook edging down 0.4% to 85.5.
The index measuring whether it was a good time to buy major household items fell 7.1% to 83.0, while unemployment expectations rose 1.9% to 142.1.
Westpac economist Matthew Hassan said previously flagged upside risks to inflation were materialising, while the RBA was also wary of demand pressures from the AI and data-centre boom.
He expects another rate hike at the RBA’s November meeting.

title: Australia Consumer Sentiment Weakens for 2nd Straight Month
